errors.claim: The Chapter 3 epigraph from Hans von Seeckt treats action as a sequence of thought, preparation, and execution governed by will; character without intellect is dangerous, but intellect without will is worthless.
errors.searches: rg 'seeckt|thoughts of a soldier'; read epigraph lines 2167-2178; note line 4334
errors.source_check: Source epigraph (lines 2169-2175) reads: 'Intellect without will is worthless, will without intellect is dangerous.' It also states 'for the man of action character is of more critical importance than intellect.' The reference's aphorism-pair swaps 'will' for 'character' in the danger clause: it says 'character without intellect is dangerous' where the source says 'WILL without intellect is dangerous.' The second clause ('intellect without will is worthless') and the three-stage/governed-by-will framing are exact. One clause term-swapped within an otherwise faithful paraphrase. Note: the consolidated lineage entry (line 626) states the von Seeckt relation generically and correctly.
